title: Read the job scope
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Identify scope, inclusions, exclusions and access windows in a work order before arrival.
Clarify contradictory or missing instructions with the coordinator before allocating time.
Produce a clarification request and workable task sequence without assuming authorisation for extra work.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Review customer instructions, inclusions, exclusions, access windows, staff eligibility and evidence requirements.

instruction.heading: Purpose and learning outcome
instruction.body: After this lesson, the learner can demonstrate read the job scope in a routine cleaning workplace, identify limits of their authority and document the result. The following procedures are examples; always apply the approved site process and task instructions.

instruction.heading: Detailed workplace method
instruction.body: Read the site address and access instructions in the authorised job system, verify the correct customer and booking window, and review scope, exclusions, priority rooms, site contacts and completion evidence. Identify dependencies such as water, power, keys, parking and other contractors. Clarify ambiguous or contradictory instructions before arrival. Do not infer consent to perform extra tasks or handle client possessions.

instruction.heading: Safety, boundaries and escalation
instruction.body: Before proceeding, confirm the actual work scope, hazards, material or equipment suitability and who can authorise changes. Stop and seek direction when work is unsafe, outside training, or the requested result conflicts with a site instruction. Record facts, not assumptions.

instruction.heading: Worked example
instruction.body: A turnover order says “full clean” but the inventory lists only bathrooms and kitchen. The cleaner contacts the coordinator to confirm whether bedrooms and linen are included before allocating time.

instruction.heading: Supervised practical
instruction.body: Review a sample work order containing missing access instructions, an unclear appliance task and a conflicting completion time; produce a clarification request and task sequence.

instruction.heading: Assessment and corrective feedback
instruction.body: An assessor observes the learner and verifies: Identifies scope and exclusions, asks timely questions and creates a workable task order without assuming authorisation. If any critical safety action is missed, provide coaching and require a new demonstration. Attendance alone is not proof of competence.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Verify the site address, access instructions, customer and booking window in the authorised job system before arrival.
Review the scope, exclusions, priority rooms, site contacts and completion evidence.
Identify dependencies such as water, power, keys, parking and other contractors.
Clarify ambiguous or contradictory instructions with the coordinator before arrival.
Confirm the work scope, the hazards and who can authorise changes before proceeding.
Build the task sequence from the clarified scope, and allocate time only once the scope is confirmed.
Do not infer consent for extra tasks or for handling client possessions.
Record facts rather than assumptions, and stop to seek direction if the work is unsafe, outside your training or conflicts with a site instruction.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: The site address, access instructions, customer and booking window are verified in the authorised job system before arrival.
Scope, exclusions, priority rooms, site contacts and completion evidence are identified from the work order.
Ambiguous or contradictory instructions are clarified before arrival, and dependencies such as water, power and keys are identified.
No consent is inferred for extra tasks or for handling client possessions.
summary: The work order is read before arrival for scope, inclusions, exclusions, access windows, staff eligibility and evidence requirements.
Contradictory or missing instructions are clarified with the coordinator before any time is allocated.
The task sequence is built from the clarified scope, and the cleaner does not assume authority for extra work.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which evidence or checks are essential when you read the job scope?
options: Whether last visit's notes are still accurate, so the check can be skipped and nothing has changed since then
The cleaner's preferred order of rooms and the time each room usually takes to clean
The job scope, exclusions, booking window and access instructions, checked in the authorised system
The client's verbal promise of extra tasks and the time the client wants to be home

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a request for work the job scope does not cover be handled?
options: Do the extra task, since the client seems happy and the extra task takes only a minute
Ask the client to choose tasks on arrival and then agree the price and the time on the spot
Clarify the ambiguity with the coordinator before arriving, and do not do the extra task without approval
Allocate the time anyway and sort it out with the client on the day and tell them the price

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when the job scope is unclear about bedrooms and linen?
options: Assume a full clean means every room, and allocate the time and tell the client on arrival
Contact the coordinator to confirm whether bedrooms and linen are included, before allocating time
Clean only the bathrooms and kitchen, since that is what the inventory lists today
Ask the cleaner on the last visit and then book the full time for the whole house

knowledgeChecks.question: Which response to a job scope request is unsafe?
options: Asking for clarification on contradictory instructions
Noting dependencies such as water, power and keys
Assuming consent to extra tasks because the client asked
Checking the access instructions in the authorised system

knowledgeChecks.question: What should be recorded about a scope question before the job starts?
options: Start work and fix the scope on the day with the client standing on site
A clarification request and a task sequence, recorded with the scope question
A verbal promise to the client about the next visit and the price
Nothing, if the cleaners know the house and the keys are on the hook
